title.en: Bridge deck, bearing interface and approaches

summary: Make a small bridge legible as deck, span members, connection interfaces, abutments and approaches rather than an unsupported curved walkway.
objective: Trace the chosen deck support arrangement in an underside view and keep traversable surfaces separate from rails, water and structural obstacles.
example_prompts: Build an inspectable footbridge with clear deck supports and continuous approaches.
Show the difference between a bearing-supported bridge and an integral connection without designing a real bridge.

principles: Choose one structural archetype before decorating: a beam span with bearings, an integral frame, an arch or a suspension system imply different connection details. The cited FHWA guidance documents both bearing and integral interfaces.
Keep deck surface, primary span members, substructure and ground interface distinguishable. Decorative rails should not visually impersonate the only load-carrying assembly.
Structural explanation and walkable collision geometry are separate layers. A deck can support a character while the underside and rails remain obstacles; water beneath it is not traversable ground.
An illustrative support arrangement must not imply verified dimensions, code compliance, structural capacity or foundation adequacy.
implementation: For an authored beam example, name deck boards/slab, two or more chosen girders, transverse ties, bearing seats and abutments. Place each span end on a visible interface; for an integral alternative, replace the bearing detail with a continuous chosen connection.
Give the deck a real thickness and distinguish top surface from soffit. Add material changes at timber, metal or masonry interfaces without forcing one style or universally prescribing brackets.

Represent bearing movement only if its allowed translation/rotation is explicitly chosen; do not animate every support in every direction. Keep a diagrammatic degrees-of-freedom overlay separate from rendered construction.

Generate approaches from the same deck-end elevations used by support queries. Specify slope/step limits for the chosen traveler, provide a bounded support search and keep water/rail exclusions active.

Use separate selectable deck, connection and substructure groups. A cutaway or lift-off view may reveal them while preserving saved assembled transforms; collider behavior must follow the declared inspection mode.

If a load slider merely changes explanatory arrows, label it schematic. A stress or displacement result requires a stated structural model, boundary conditions and an independently checked calculation.
observable_checks: From below, each chosen girder end reaches its bearing seat or declared integral joint; none terminates in air.
Trace a traveler from bank to approach to deck to opposite bank: support height is continuous within the declared limits and water below is rejected.
Move an inspection slider out and back: deck, supports and labels return to the same assembly, with no hidden duplicate collision plane.
Switch between the authored bearing and integral variants: connection labels and permitted-motion overlays change together.

known_limits: FHWA source supports interface classification; this record does not certify bearings, fasteners, foundations or any pedestrian/vehicle load.
Traverse checks apply to the chosen collision/support model, not accessibility or construction approval.
Authored modeling guidance and prospective checks; no runtime artifact has been executed for this record.
creative_affordances: Use timber, stone, metal, glass or fictional materials and vary span silhouette; choose a matching support explanation instead of enforcing a universal bridge style.

claims.statement: FHWA describes structural bearings at superstructure/substructure connections and also documents integral connections as an alternative.
claims.scope: Connection classification in FHWA PBES guidance, sections 2.5 and 2.5.4; no claim that every bridge needs separate bearings.

source_refs.locator: Sections 2.5 Connections between Superstructures and Substructures and 2.5.4 Structural Bearings.
